review: Fresh independent ordinary visible playtest; normal http://127.0.0.1:5173/; exactly two terminal attempts
scale: 0 unusable/absent; 2 severely weak; 4 rough prototype; 5 functional but substantial shortcomings; 6 promising vertical slice; 7 strong indie quality; 8 polished commercial quality; 9 excellent AAA quality; 10 exceptional benchmark. AAA-readiness measures readiness for a full-price AAA release, not ambition. Ratings reflect observed scope only.

gameplay.reason: Induction optic kill is satisfying; recovery supplies and route choice create stakes. First attempts were dominated by navigation around cover and attritional fire; shift did not produce a successful evade in my play. Two deaths give insufficient evidence for encounter depth or late balance.

presentation.reason: Cohesive storm-lit teal/amber industrial identity, strong title/death typography and attractive Heart silhouette. Blocky repeated robots/props and sparse spatial detail retain a prototype appearance.

usability.reason: Controls remain discoverable on HUD; paused selectable map works and fresh restart resets cleanly. Receiver reach required trial and error, and nearby/behind-cover guidance did not make the last approach obvious to me.

readability.reason: Large health/ammo and optic color are clear; distance markers and named signs help. Small condensed HUD text, layered guidance, obstructing cover and offscreen fire make situational reading harder.

AAA-readiness.reason: Strong visual direction and functional slice, but observed repetition, modest geometry/animation, rough approach clarity and narrow unverified mission coverage fall well short of release-grade AAA proof.
